Figure 9:Real-robot setup.(1) Fixed head camera (Intel RealSense D455f), (2) wrist camera (Innomaker U20CAM), (3) reBot arm, and (4) 1 m conveyor.
Colored stickers make belt motion visible.
Arrow: belt direction.
Both camera images are provided at224×224224\times 224, and the arm is controlled at 20 Hz.
The image shows the start of a sponge-picking trial.

Figure 11:Gripper position during real-conveyor picking.One trial per policy and speed, both policies using past frames, shown from the head camera when the gripper first closes.
Each trial is closest to the median closing time among its 10 trials; Fast-WAM never closes at 0.20 m/s, so its last frame is shown.
Dashed outline: sponge.
Arrow: belt direction, shorter at the slower speed.

Figure S3:Success rate per skill category and belt speedfor the eight policies with past frames (number of tasks in parentheses; each cell pools the category’s tasks, 20 episodes per task and speed).
Dots: the speed of highest success in each row; rows without a success have none.

Figure S9:The three real-robot tasksat the start of a trial: (1) “Pick the yellow sponge”, with the sponge on the belt; (2) “Place the red cube in the plate”, with the cube in the gripper and the plate on the belt; (3) “Push the apple off the belt”.
A trial is completed if the sponge is grasped, the cube rests on the plate, or the apple falls off the belt.
Figure S11:All 80 tasks, grouped by skill category, one frame each from a scripted-expert demonstration, rendered without the randomized table and background.
